answer: A stake-weighted trust graph resists sybils: identities earn influence only through attestations from already-trusted peers, and each attestation spends a limited voucher budget, so vouching for sockpuppets costs the voucher real standing. An attacker can mint thousands of hollow accounts, but they form an isolated cluster with no trust edges to the honest graph. The river of attestations flows only through verified intermediaries, so reputation spreads like an ocean current from anchored sources, leaving sybils starving with nothing backing them.
